title: Microservices Patterns
summary: The vocabulary of building distributed systems as services — decomposition, communication, API gateways, resilience patterns, transactional messaging, sagas, CQRS, event sourcing, service mesh, testing, deployment, and the 2026 landscape (modular monoliths, function mesh, multi-runtime, Wasm).

volatileChapters.reason: Modular-monolith counter-trend + multi-runtime (Dapr) + Wasm components evolve quarterly; agent-as-microservice is brand-new.

inspiredBy.title: Microservices Patterns (Chris Richardson) + Building Microservices (Sam Newman)

chapters.title: Decomposition
chapters.summary: Breaking a monolith — decomposition by business capability vs by subdomain, the strangler fig migration pattern, identifying service boundaries, and the cost of premature service boundaries.

chapters.title: Communication Patterns
chapters.summary: How services talk — synchronous (REST, gRPC, GraphQL) vs asynchronous (messaging); request/response vs event-driven; the latency/coupling trade-offs and when each fits.

chapters.title: API Gateway and BFF
chapters.summary: The edge layer — API Gateway responsibilities (routing, auth, rate limiting, aggregation), the Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) pattern, the GraphQL gateway approach, and the gateway anti-patterns.

chapters.title: Service Discovery
chapters.summary: Finding service instances — client-side (Eureka, Ribbon) vs server-side (kube-proxy, ELB) discovery, DNS-based (CoreDNS), config-service-backed (Consul, etcd, ZooKeeper), and health-check integration.

chapters.title: Resilience Patterns
chapters.summary: Surviving partial failure — circuit breaker (closed/open/half-open), bulkhead, timeout, retry with exponential backoff and jitter, idempotency keys, and the layered defense approach.

chapters.title: Transactional Messaging
chapters.summary: Reliable async — the dual-write problem, the outbox pattern, transaction log tailing (CDC), message deduplication, the idempotent receiver, and exactly-once-effectively semantics.

chapters.title: The Saga Pattern
chapters.summary: Long-running multi-service transactions — choreography vs orchestration, compensating transactions, saga participants, the saga state machine, and the trade-offs vs 2PC.

chapters.title: CQRS
chapters.summary: Command-Query Responsibility Segregation — separating write models from read models, projections, eventual consistency between them, when to apply CQRS, and when not to.

chapters.title: Event Sourcing
chapters.summary: State as a log of events — append-only event log, replay to rebuild state, snapshots, projections, temporal queries, schema evolution challenges, and the audit-log win.

chapters.title: Service Mesh
chapters.summary: L7 infrastructure as code — the sidecar proxy pattern, mTLS between services, traffic shaping (canary, mirror), retries and timeouts at the mesh layer, and observability without code changes (Istio, Linkerd, Cilium).

chapters.title: Testing Microservices
chapters.summary: Test pyramid for distributed systems — unit, integration, contract testing (Pact, consumer-driven contracts), component tests, end-to-end tests, service virtualization, and the testing-in-production pattern.

chapters.title: Deploying Microservices
chapters.summary: Independent deployability — deployment topology (per-service pipelines), blue/green per service, canary at the service level, rollback strategies, schema migration coordination, and the deployment manifest pattern.

chapters.title: Microservices in 2026
chapters.summary: The current landscape — modular monoliths counter-trend (Shopify pattern), function mesh (Lambda + Step Functions), multi-runtime apps (Dapr), Wasm components for polyglot microservices, and AI agents as a new microservice archetype.
